newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Surinam ex-leader blasts Dutch on arrest warrant.
newsitem.headline: Surinam ex-leader blasts Dutch on arrest warrant.

text.p: Surinam's former military leader Desi Bouterse on Tuesday denied drug trafficking and blasted the Netherlands, the former colonial power in Surinam, for seeking his arrest for alleged drug smuggling.
The burly 51-year-old ex-army sergeant who ruled Surinam throughout the 1980s told RFO Guyane television in an interview that the Dutch were motivated by politics rather than drugs.

"Since the 1980s they have always been looking for something against me. Before they called me a communist, then an assassin, and these days I'm a drug baron. All of this is done systematically on a political basis," Bouterse said.
"This is a long story, since the 1980s we in Surinam started a real decolonisation movement and since then it has not been in the interest of the Netherlands," he said.
The interview was conducted in the Surinam capital Paramaribo on Sunday and made available to Reuters on Tuesday.
Surinam announced earlier on Tuesday that it was recalling its ambassador from the Netherlands following the Dutch government's decision to seek Bouterse's arrest and extradition.
The Dutch request for police assistance to detain Bouterse has strained already tense diplomatic ties between the two nations.

Bouterse, who no longer holds public office but is an adviser to Surinam's current president Jules Wijdenbosch, said the Surinamese government had not received formal notification of a demand for his extradition.
He said Dutch police were using scare tactics to try to force drug traffickers held in Dutch prisons to implicate him.
"In Dutch prisons, authorities promise reductions in sentences and residence papers to prisoners on drug charges if they implicate me in drug trafficking," Bouterse said.
"I have nothing to do with drug trafficking (though) there is some drug trafficking in Surinam from other South American countries," he said.

The Netherlands said last week it was seeking international cooperation to arrest Bouterse and the Dutch Justice Ministry said a request for Bouterse's arrest had been filed with the Interpol international police organisation.
Dutch Justice Ministry spokesman Victor Holtus said the move was linked to an ongoing criminal investigation into allegations that Bouterse was involved in large-scale cocaine smuggling.
The head of the Dutch public prosecution service said earlier this year that he expected to bring charges against Bouterse in several months.
Bouterse has been distrusted by the Netherlands since he led Surinam's 600-strong army into overthrowing a civilian goverment in 1980.

During the following decade the country was torn by civil war that left hundreds dead out of a population of 400,000. Over 15,000 ethnic "Bush Negroes" fled into adjacent French Guiana, a French overseas department.
In 1982, Bouterse was accused by the Dutch government of ordering the summary execution of 15 politcal opposition leaders.
Observers view Bouterse as retaining strong political influence in Surinam since Wijdenbosch, a long-time Bouterse ally, was elected president last year.
Independent from the Netherlands since 1975, Surinam's economy has suffered from over 15 years of political instability.
